page: Amazon Web Services r5n.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz across 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are coupled with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, while offering a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance in mid-to-lower performance tiers across general compute and memory evaluations. In Geekbench testing, the single-core rating achieved 1179.0 points, categorized as average, while multi-core performance registered 2596.0 points in the lower 25% bracket. PassMark metrics reflect a similar profile, yielding an average memory score of 2073.43 alongside a CPU score of 3958.04. Memory bandwidth testing shows 27.6 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 23.38 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific operations measured 3.36 million operations per second for Redis SET requests and 3.74 GB/sec for static web serving.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of RAM relative to assigned compute cores. Without high-end CPU benchmarks, the hardware allocation targets workloads constrained by physical memory size rather than sustained processing speed. Operational tradeoffs include the complete absence of local non-volatile storage, making all persistence dependent on EBS bandwidth and latency. Given these hardware specifications and performance metrics, Amazon Web Services r5n.xlarge functions effectively for memory-heavy operations, in-memory caches such as Redis, moderate relational databases, and data processing tasks requiring substantial addressable working memory.
